description: The line plot compares the performance of six different methods across varying co-occurrence numbers. The x-axis is labeled "Co-occurrence Number" and employs a logarithmic scale with major tick marks labeled at 0, $10^1$, $10^2$, and $10^3$. The y-axis is labeled "ACC (%)" and uses a linear scale with a visible range from 40 to 65, featuring tick marks at intervals of 5 units. The plot contains six solid lines, each with distinct colors and markers, plotted across four discrete data points along the x-axis. The "Base" method is represented by a black line with circle markers, starting at an accuracy of approximately 38, rising steadily to about 43.5 at the third data point, and ending at roughly 44. The "FT" method is shown as a blue line with downward-pointing triangle markers, beginning at approximately 40 and increasing steadily to end at roughly 47.5. The "IKE" method uses a red line with upward-pointing triangle markers, starting at about 43 and rising to end at approximately 49.5. The "MEND" method is depicted by a brown line with diamond markers, starting at roughly 44.5, increasing to 54 at the third data point, and finishing at about 56.5. The "MEMIT" method is represented by a purple line with hexagon markers, beginning at approximately 43.5, rising to 51 at the second data point, and ending at roughly 54.5. Finally, a series with a redacted legend label (covered by a solid gray rectangle) is shown as a green line with square markers; it exhibits the highest values throughout, starting at approximately 51, increasing to 62.5 at the third data point, and reaching a maximum of roughly 66 at the final data point. All lines demonstrate an upward trend from the left to the right side of the plot.
